correctness.rationale: For normal y, compress ad_y^m(a)=0 to two disjoint compact spectral sets. The Sylvester map between these spectral subspaces is invertible by spectral separation, so the off-diagonal block vanishes. Regularity extends this to disjoint Borel sets and proves that a commutes with all spectral projections; a faithful representation gives the C*-algebra version. Now ad_a([a,b])=0 and the Kleinecke–Shirokov implication makes y quasinilpotent, hence zero by normality. Independently the uniformity argument can use the bounded product modulo the c0-sum: a sequence of contraction pairs with both defects tending to zero and commutator norms bounded below would give an exact nonzero normal counterexample in the quotient, whose norm is the limsup. Taking the supremum over contraction pairs yields the stated nondecreasing modulus; scaling gives exponents 4 and 2m+1. The Calkin quotient makes both compact defects exactly zero, giving compactness. For the exact-relation corollary one can also argue directly: any nonzero spectral point of compact Y has a finite-rank Riesz projection P; spectral separation on the P and 1−P ranges gives Pa=aP by the same Sylvester argument (with A as first factor). The restricted commutator has trace zero, but Y on that range has trace λ rank(P), ruling out λ≠0. For N with a single infinite-rank off-diagonal identity block, N²=0, ad_N³=0 and [N*,N]=diag(−I,I). Thus I+εN has norm at least one, normality defect ε² and exact weakened relation at m≥3. Brown–Pearcy gives commutator existence since εN is noncompact and no nonzero scalar shift of I+εN can be compact. Bounded products along any sequence would balance both factors by reciprocal scalings and contradict the modulus. The finite-rank matrix-unit example confirms that exactness cannot be omitted for quasinilpotence.
residual_risks: This is a qualitative modulus at fixed m, not a rate or an optimal exponent.
The boundary model is only asserted for m≥3, not a failure at m=2; the compactness statement alone gives no spectral conclusion outside the essential spectrum.

Credit the boundary only as a limiting obstruction to dropping a uniform factor bound, not as a new existence theorem.

value.rationale: The two nonzero defects quantify exactly which approximations are allowed when an inner derivation is generated by the unknown commutator itself. The bound is uniform for growing matrix dimensions and arbitrary unital C*-algebras, and forces compactness under strictly weaker modulo-compact information than an exact relation on the original operators. The boundary identifies why merely bounded individual factorizations are insufficient, without mistaking almost-normality alone for rigidity.
residual_risks: The method is qualitative and not directly a numerical tolerance prescription; the obstruction is only given for m≥3.
